Audit · MX17 micromegas · June-2026 cosmic bench · raw DREAM ADC

The June boards’ X view moves charge straight from one neighbour to the other. Its cause is open: a pull onto narrow resistive strips did it in a 1-D toy, but not in the full sim

A fresh look at a week of work, updated the same evening: the observation is solid and well mapped, and many causes are firmly excluded. The size is set by the cloud width alone (not gain, not time). The sharing test first thought to exclude registration does not decide it. Narrow strips with a charged-gap funnel, which reach the data’s size in a 1-D toy, give a smaller asymmetry than the production strips in the full sim.

2

Details

Observable: per event, the peak X channel n and its neighbours n±1. α is the in-phase content (each neighbour waveform projected on the central pulse), so it is a charge fraction, insensitive to small timing shifts. a1 > 0 means DAQ channel n+1 carries more than n−1. With uniform illumination and a symmetric response, a1 = 0 on average.

Extractor: raw_asym.py (pedestal-subtracted DREAM ADC, DAQ channel numbers, no strip map, no common-mode subtraction, no clustering, no M3). Good-pulse cut 200 < A_c < 3500, central peak sample 4–22, quiet pre-samples. Matched X/Y events by (file, eventId) in scratchpad/2026-10-20/r5/r5lib.py; channels within 4 of a connector edge cut.

The strips run along y on every May and June build (the slow, along-strip view is Y on all of them); det0/det1 run the other way.

3

Details

Local size = sqrt(mean(cell mean²) − mean(cell error²)) over the 8 × 8 map (64 × 64 columns × rows per cell, ≥ 25 events), i.e. the typical |a1| in a cell beyond statistical noise, whatever its sign. det2’s field is as strong as det3’s but changes sign in bands, so its board mean is zero. That is why det2 served as a "copy-free control" until the maps were made (route 23), and why several early conclusions that used it are re-checked later in this deck.

A small common a1Y ≈ −0.01 appears on quiet and June boards alike: an instrumental baseline.

Source: audit_data.py (r5lib matched events, edge cut).

Details

Constant-model χ²/ndf of the X maps (8 × 8): det3 June-15 332/63, det2 736/61, det6 47/25, det7 21/8; controls det3 May 78/56, det1 34/27. Y maps: det3 June-15 74/63, det2 59/61. The main session’s 4 × 4 maps by pad class (Y-pad class): det3 X 438/15 vs Y 30/15; det2 X 971/15 vs Y 21/15; det2’s X-pad-class map is flat (15/15).

det2’s two runs (6-17 FEU 3, 6-22 FEU 6) show the same bands; det3’s two FEU-3 sessions give the same map phase at different amplitude. det4 changes sign across x. No step at any of the 7 connector boundaries (det3: every step ≤ 0.02 ± 0.03).

Caveat: these maps pool sessions. det3’s cloud width also varies across x (Y share 0.89 at chip 0 to 0.48 at chip 7), and the amplitude depends on the width, so the map shape is the field times a width pattern. A per-session, width-matched map is on the to-do list.

Details

6

Details

Main session, scratchpad/2026-10-21/m3class/ (ysh_class.py, ysh_class_sim.py, m3_align.py). The old label (p_x + p_y) % 2 uses the X peak; when n+1 outgrows n the peak moves, the label flips, and the event lands in the other class with a large negative a1. M3 can’t give an X-independent column (pointing 0.9–2.0 mm at the detector vs 0.78 mm pads). The Y share s can: on det3 May the Y-pad fraction falls 0.80 (s < 0.3) → 0.35 (1.25–1.5) → 0.20 (> 1.5).

det3 June-15 over all events: +0.17 / +0.19 at s < 0.3, +0.11 … +0.14 at 0.5–1.0, +0.15 / +0.18 at s > 1.25. An effect only over the Y pads would fall 3–4×. det2’s positive band falls mildly at s > 1.1 (+0.10 / +0.03 ± 0.04, few events).

Consequences: anything tied to the Y pads (vias, Y-pad copper, the bus beside the Y pads, Y→X transfer) is excluded; the "lives at the Y pads" reading (route 11) is overturned; every model score built on A_Y / A_X by X-peak class (routes 12, 13, 15–17, 26 and the floating-strip rejection, route 9) tested size convolved with migration, not location. The sim arms are also flat in s (±0.03 per bin) and reproduce the label artefact, so this does not discriminate between them.

The Y view is flat in both label classes too (main session, yview/yview_class.py): det3 June-15 a1Y −0.002 / −0.003 ± 0.004; Y-pad-label map X 438/15 vs Y 30/15.

7

Details

Integrals of positive samples per channel (r5/probe_charge.py). On det3 June-15 Y-pad events n+1 carries 0.216 of ΣY and n−1 only 0.116; det3 May has 0.160 / 0.163. A plain copy x(n+1) += a·x(n) would raise n+1 without lowering n−1 (and raise the central), so this is not a copy (route 10).

Route 14 (Y→X transfer: a floating or cracked-via Y pad, Y-line crosstalk, bus pickup) was first checked against det2, which carries the field and has a different gain ratio (ΣX/ΣY spans 0.86–1.01 across boards). Redone within one board: a transfer of ≈ the n+1 − n−1 excess (0.10 of ΣY) would raise the Y-pad class above the X-pad class. Instead it is lower (0.907 vs 0.925). Excluded without any reference board.

8

Details

det2 (even/det2_profile.py, 32 cells, a1 −0.30 … +0.26, Y share and Y ±2 as width controls): per unit a1, −0.54 / +0.47 at ∓1, −0.08 / +0.04 at ∓2, ~0 at ∓3. det3 June-15 − May (even/antisym.py, Y-share bins 0.6–1.05, odd part): the same shape, with ±2 at ~1/4 of ±1. Operators applied to May’s mean profile and scaled to the measured Δa1: a nearest-neighbour antisymmetric coupling dq_n = (ε/2)(q_{n−1} − q_{n+1}) puts ~40 % of the ±1 change at ±2; a copy dq_n = a·q_{n−1} raises n+1 and gives n−1 nothing.

So it isn’t a fixed linear channel operator (consistent with the failed mixing fits, route 5). It depends on where the charge sits, i.e. a position-level mechanism; a pull toward the strips is one. The May → June-15 ±2/±3 even drop (−0.05 / −0.02) is mostly a bulk difference (e.g. the photon-feedback halo): det2’s within-board even slope predicts only −0.01 at a1 = 0.14.

Strip-pull toy (loop/toy_shape.py, the attractor toy of slide "Even term"): at the data’s operating point (a1 0.10–0.20 with |Δs1| ≤ 0.03 vs no pull) the ±2 odd part is 0.01–0.14 of the ±1 one (σ 450 µm: 0.10–0.14) with a small negative ±2 even part, like det2. Shown: 30% of the charge pulled onto lines 300 µm off the pad centres, σ 450 µm clouds, 200 µm induction: a1 +0.163, Δs1 +0.003. ±3 is not computed in the toy (drawn at 0). This toy pulls part of the whole cloud to the line nearest its centre, which a linear detector can’t do; it is a shape check, and slide “Physical pull” has the per-electron version.

9

Details

Noise test (noise_corr_inject.py): quiet events, common mode removed; the correlation between channels at distance 1 minus distance 2. An electronic copy (FEU, ADC mux, cable) copies noise too: injecting x(n) += A·x(n−1) into the real noise raises the excess by +0.06…0.12 at A = 0.1. det3 X measures +0.03 / −0.03 / −0.02, the same as boards without the effect.

Connector edge (raw_asym.py --edge, edge_test.py): at a connector’s lowest column, the physical neighbour col−1 is on another connector, cable and DREAM chip. a1 there (+0.21 ± 0.03) equals the inside value; the DAQ neighbour on the same chip (127 columns away) gets nothing. On 6-28 (FEU 7) it is +0.03 ± 0.03 vs +0.09 inside, a 2σ difference.

With the two-signed field, these exclude the electronics, connectors, M1 card and any fixed copper layout (bus traces, stubs, vias: one sign everywhere).

10

Details

Sessions: 6-18 long run and 6-19/20 longer run are EOS extractions (FEU 7, X only); 6-22/23 and 6-23/24 FEU 3 (drift 1000 / 600 V); 6-25 drift 500 V; 6-27 drift scan (1100 → 100 V: a1 rose 0.05 → 0.16, back to the 1000 V value right after, i.e. reversible); 6-27/28 FEU 7. The n_TOF beam run_79 (July 26, Ar/iso 90/10) gives 0.05–0.07 with the older whole-board method.

A fixed map × one scale per session fits det3 (0.96 / 1.57 / 0.44; χ² 47/60, 126/61, 47/59), and det2’s two runs differ by ×2.5 with the same bands (median Y share 0.35 vs 1.07).

Within a night the trend is not there (dotted lines, all events): the per-event Y share mostly says which pad type the charge sits on, and a1 is the same over both. The older "one curve" (a1 of Y-pad-labelled events vs Y share, all sessions on one curve) used the X-peak labels, whose migration grows as the Y share falls, so it overstated the per-event width dependence. What survives is night-to-night: median Y share 0.52 / 0.77 / 0.93 with a1 +0.18 / +0.14 / +0.10 (sess_width.py), plus the drift scan and det2’s two runs.

6-19/20 was det2 (s619/): the "det3 FEU 7" data (a1 0.03, all 8 chips lit) has det2’s readout-chain noise pattern (r = 0.957 with det2 X on 6-22) and not det3’s on the same FEU 7 slot on 6-17; the pattern follows chain + board, not the FEU slot. det3’s X readout lit only chips 0–3 on 6-17, and on 6-19 that 4-chip readout is the FEU 3 file: 372 events, a1 +0.077 ± ~0.03 (≈ 2σ low, few events). The raw_daq_data HV scan + long run could add more.

11

Details

time/time_a1.py. Charging-up of insulating surfaces scales with the deposited charge (gain × rate) and builds over minutes to hours. At fixed width the resist scans change the central amplitude ~×6 (6-23: 525 → 465 V) with a1 flat at 0.15–0.21; 6-22’s 8-hour scan and 6-27 afternoon → overnight show no drift. Runs where most pulses rail (6-22 at 505–525 V) or sit below ~400 ADC are dropped from the left panel. The 6-23/24 step at 490 V coincides with a width change (median Y share 0.49 → 0.57), as the right panel’s single curve expects.

Retraction: a "5× jump at fixed HV on 6-23" seen briefly in the survey table came from its copy-model estimator, which misreads low-amplitude runs; on the direct a1 the three 495 V / 600 V runs are +0.06 ± 0.05, +0.16 ± 0.02, +0.19 ± 0.01.

Details

r5/timing_width.py: the cloud_basics §42 estimator (nTof_x17) on the same events. Pulse width mixes track angle (inclined → longer), drift speed and session, so the quartiles are not pure angle bins. Route 21’s "prompt" and §42’s "delayed 114 ns" are the same data under different angle mixes (route 39).

Only the anisotropic-strip sim (σxx = 10 σyy, one tuned parameter) reproduces the sign swing; its Y view was not computed (the hybrids keep the production isotropic Y kernels).

13

Details

2026-10-22/cloud/ (MX17_Geant). The 10-21 near-vertical cut keeps central FWHM ≥ the set’s own 25th percentile. The data’s pulses are short (det3 May X |Δt| < 30 ns: median 423 ns; sim 590 ns), so that cut compared different populations. In absolute FWHM bins det3 May X matches the baseline sim (shape χ² 23.9 / 18 on the cells every arm fills). Dry-gas D_T is excluded by the time profile (86 / 18); depth-independent clouds (no diffusion, σ0 250 / 400 µm) fail (565 / 57); σ0 400 µm (17.5) and feedback spread 400 µm (19.0) are no better than the baseline.

The short pulses are not small x-tilts: sheared th00 tracks at 1–3° and Stage A thx05/thx10 almost never pass |Δt| < 80 ns, and those that do have lower early sharing. They are partial drift columns (late onset or early end), 29–43 % of det3 May’s sample, 62–84 % of det3 June-15’s, 1–4 % of the sim’s. What makes them: next slide (§12).

14

Details

2026-10-22/partial/ (MX17_Geant), M3 tracks joined by eventId (Chi2X, Chi2Y < 5). The view X ↔ M3 y mapping holds in May too (chip medians). det3 May: the |Δt(n+1 − n−1)| < 80 ns sample keeps inclined tracks; FWHM < 350 ns pulses have |θ_meas| 6.3° (long 1.3°). With M3 |θ| < 2° only 11 % are short.

det3 June 6-23 (the d3jun reference, every 600 V sub-run): per vertical muon the column arrives as a ~0.5 µs burst at a random depth (onset p10–p90 4–15 samples, end flat 9–31); X and Y (FEU 3 and 4) agree event by event (onset r = 0.83); det4 in the same events is uncorrelated (r = 0.04), so not the trigger; 95 % have the M3 track on the hit chip, so not other particles; uniform over angle, board position, M3 multiplicity and time in the run; no dropped-sample floors. 9-pad amplitude 4–5× below the other sessions and nearly flat over the 465–525 V resist scan (×1.5 vs ×8 on 6-27); α+1 0.08–0.2 vs 0.3–0.47. HV readback normal (600 V, 495 V; resist current 0.62 vs ~1.1 µA). Not the drift field: 6-25 at 500 V and the 6-27 scan at 500–1100 V have sharp column ends. Mechanism open (a resistive layer not following its supply, i.e. charging, fits the flat gain; electron loss in the gas does not explain random depths).

Step 2: clean det3 June X (6-27 long_run + overnight, 1000 V = sim) at matched absolute FWHM: χ² 34 / 16 vs the sim (det3 May 121 / 36, 6-23 639 / 24); late growth not suppressed (2.02 vs sim 1.87). Early sharing sits above the sim on both boards alike (May 0.83, June 0.78, sim 0.58). So §8–10’s "det3 June prompt-wide, flat, suppressed late growth" fingerprint is the 6-23 session, not the June bulk. The asymmetry itself is in the clean sessions (survey a ≈ 0.07–0.11).

15

Details

2026-10-22/partial/slot_table.py, scan617.py, det2_rescore.py, board_vs_board.py. Board names: physical boards as in copy_survey (the 6-17 run_config’s descriptions are swapped). Both degraded nights put the board in the bottom slot (z 232 mm) on drift 0:7 and resist 3:3, but the same slot and channels were healthy on 6-22 (det3, slower columns), 6-25 (det3) and 6-26 (det6), so it is a per-night condition, not the slot. HV readback normal where logged. A resistive layer not following its supply (bad contact, floating) fits the flat gain; nothing here tests it. The bench logbook for 6-17 and 6-23 is the next check.

det2’s §8 timing used 6-22 (clean). Re-scored with the same cells as det3: near the sim, prompt sharing not narrower than the sim’s, late growth slightly above it. The §8 statement “det2 narrow-prompt / late-wide, det3 June the opposite” is reduced to a ≤ 2σ difference between two sim-like boards: timing no longer constrains the strip routes either way.

The print film: 761 µm pitch, fill 0.69 (the spec’s 550 / 800 shape), a very regular print

Five phone macro photos with a steel ruler; strip edges (red) and mm ticks (green) found automatically; red points: pitch per photo

Same pitch at 31 and 73–93 px/mm: the ruler’s height above the film does not bias it (≤ 0.5 %). Lens distortion leaves ±1 % (the middle third of every frame reads ~10 µm low). Strip-to-strip placement jitter 6–10 µm.

16

Details

2026-10-22/strip_photo/ (MX17_Geant): level.py levels each photo on the ruler edge, measure.py maps x to mm with a cubic fit to the mm ticks, takes the scale’s change with image row from the strips’ own pitch, and finds strip edges at the local mid-level. Photos: Dylan, 2026-10-22, the strip pattern printed on a transparency.

Result: pitch 760.7 µm (photo spread 2.3 µm, ±1 % distortion systematic), dark 528 µm / clear 242 µm, fill 0.694 ± 0.016 (spec 550 / 800 = 0.6875). If the film is 1:1, the as-built pitch is 761 µm, not 800: against 780 µm pads that beats with a period 761 × 780 / 19 ≈ 31.2 mm, the same superperiod as the 800 µm design, with the registration drifting the other way. If the film is a scaled print (95 %) of the 800 µm design, the shape is exactly the spec. Which it is decides whether the sim needs anything new.

A ruler-free strip count across the whole film (overview photo, phase unwrapping; 499 strips for 800 µm vs 512 for 780 µm vs 525 for 761 µm over the active width) scattered ±20 between columns (reflections, low contrast): inconclusive.

If the film is the true pattern, the strips cannot make the asymmetry: the offset recurs every 30 mm, and the ripple that implies is absent

Strips 761 µm vs pads 780 µm: offset +19.3 µm per column, beat 30.7 mm (39 columns), 13 beats per board. Points: data, largest ripple in f = 0.015–0.036/column (grey bar: 95 % of the null)

Registration (attractor or skewed response) is a function of the strip offset only; it averages to ~0 over one beat. Only a 780 µm print could hold a board-scale field.

The sim’s strip imprint (0.127 in s1) is ≥ 5–10× the data’s on every board with the statistics, det3 May included.

17

Details

2026-10-22/film761/consequences.py (MX17_Geant), FOLLOWUP §15. B: the full sim’s a1(δ) and s1(δ) (r5/sim_delta.json) laid onto 512 columns at every starting offset; C: per-column means of s1 and a1 (detrended, σ 30 columns), first harmonic, permutation null of the column means, the same estimator as r5/beat_col.py. det3 May’s s1 peaks sit at 1/64 per column (the chip period) and show in its Y control view. det4/6/7: too few events per column.

Under the assumption that the film is the production print: strip routes (registration, offset strips, width/funnel/anisotropy levers) are out; the sim is too strip-sensitive; what remains is pad-locked or column-independent and X-only (surface charge on fresh June bulks, the June PCB pad/via layer, the bulk process). If the film were a scaled printout, the 800 µm design gives the same numbers; only a production pitch of exactly 780 µm would reopen registration.

Details

The pattern: every conclusion that matters for the exclusions survives a within-board or det3-May redo. What doesn’t survive are fine-grained model scores that subtracted det2 as a baseline and the fast-model exclusions.

One leftover from the copy model: NB_ASYM §2 used the det3 X side with share 0.30 as "copy-free" and concluded the sims overshare (v4c 0.39). Under "charge moved" that side is depleted; the symmetric value is ~0.36, which v5a (0.35) already matches. Sim targets for the X ±1 share and width should come from det3 May / det1. uncopy.py assumes the copy model and should be retired in favour of wft.xasym.

The June boards conduct across their strip gaps, but uniformly: the field doesn’t follow

a1 (red, left axis) and the across-strip late charge (green, right axis) per band

20

Details

The late ±2 content in the across-strip view (X) is the only physical June-vs-May difference found in the data: June boards 12–31 ×10⁻³ (det2 12, det3 June-15 27, det6 31), May and earlier 1–9 (det3 May 8.5, det4 May 0.8). The sim reproduces it with a gap conductance of 5–10 % of the strips’ (route 34).

New in the audit (late_vs_a1.py): inside det2 it stays 8–13 in every band while a1 runs −0.21 → +0.16 → −0.11; on det3 27–32 while a1 runs 0.09 → 0.22. Across boards det6 has the most leak and a weak field, det2 the least leak and a strong field. So conduction is a June-build marker, not what sets the local size or sign. This now rests on data, not only on the sim.

The leading candidate, strip registration, predicts an even partner to a1

Left: strips offset by δ pull the cloud; right: the full sim (strips at 800 µm over 780 µm pads) per δ bin

a1 (odd in δ)

s1 − s1(δ=0) (even in δ)

21

Details

Registration: if the strip centres sit δ off the pad columns and charge evens out across a strip quickly, narrow clouds are pulled toward the strip centre. a1 ∝ sin(2πδ/P) and the field geometry follows from the print’s scale and rotation errors (det3 ~0.07 % scale + ~0.25 mrad; det2 ~2 mrad rotation → bands ~P/θ ≈ 390 mm apart). It explains X only, charge moved, pad-pitch locking and the width dependence.

Requires a strip pitch commensurate with 780 µm; the quoted pitch is 800 µm ("borrowed from another detector"). With 800 µm the sim predicts a 31.2 mm beat of amplitude 0.12 on every board, which no board shows (≤ 0.03).

Sim table: r5/sim_delta.py (36k X-only events, xo0 th00 + thy*, seeds 5–16). s1 is 0.63 at δ ≈ 0 and 0.77–1.14 near the gaps; a fit over |δ| ≤ 275 µm gives s1 = 0.64 + 2.2 |a1|.

Details

Odd amplitude O = ⟨sgn δ · a1⟩ over |δ| ≥ 50 µm (r5/paired_odd.py), each arm paired event-for-event with the same (angle, seed) control. Grid control glg0 = ×0.95 of the production arm. Leaky gaps: a kernel-level ×1.9 became ×0.9 in the full sim (the gain arrives late). Low ρ_s: ×2.1–2.4 and the data’s timing trend, but the charge runs along the strips over many rows and the Y view loses its compact clusters.

Anisotropic strips (A = 10) give the data’s timing swing; the Y-box solve (64 families) that would check the Y view has not been run.

Details

Correction (2026-10-21 evening). The first version of this deck said the sharing (the even term) excludes registration "×20". That compared the sharing at large |a1| with the sharing at δ = 0 inside the same attractor (the sim’s s1 = 0.64 + 2.2 |a1| fit, and the det2 cell regression). An attractor narrows the cluster most at δ = 0 and leaves it about unchanged near δ = P/2, while a1 is zero at both. Measured against an unpulled board, a pull at offsets between the a1 maximum and P/2 gives a1 0.1–0.3 with Δs1 ≈ 0.

Same PCB (even/same_pcb.py): det3 May and June-15 X sharing at matched Y share differ by -0.000 ± 0.006 over the inner bins while a1 goes 0 → 0.14: consistent with no pull, or with a pull sampled around the a1 maximum. Toy: loop/toy_loop.py (pad response box ⊗ 200 µm Gaussian, pulled charge smeared 200 µm, peak-pad selection, uniform positions). The 25 sim arms’ E/O = 1.2–2.5 (even/sim_even.py) is the same within-attractor contrast, not an exclusion.

The June boards trace the loop a sweeping offset predicts, but the quiet board’s sharing varies as much

Per 64-column band: a1 (red) and the X sharing residual s1X − F(s1Y) (blue; F = the board’s own binned X-vs-Y relation)

a1

sharing residual (width removed)

24

Details

An attractor whose offset δ sweeps across a board (print scale or rotation) gives a1 ∝ sin φ and a sharing change ∝ −cos φ: the sharing residual should cross zero where a1 peaks and be extreme where a1 crosses zero. det3 June-15 does exactly that across x (+0.08 → 0.01 at the a1 maximum → −0.11). det2 by y (16 bands): +0.08 at its rising a1 zero crossing, about 0 near the extrema, −0.04 … −0.08 at the falling crossing. det4 by x: +0.08 / +0.05 / −0.19 with a1 0.03 / 0.11 / 0.03.

But det3 May, the same PCB with no asymmetry, has residuals of −0.15 and +0.13 in adjacent bands, so bulk-local sharing structure (gap, gain) is as large as the loop. June-15 doesn’t repeat May’s pattern, so it isn’t the PCB or the electronics. The loop is suggestive, not evidence (loop/det2_crossings_np.py).

In a 1-D toy a physical pull reaches the data’s size onto narrow strips; the full sim does not

Left: 1-D toy, gaps charged to saturation funnel every gap electron onto the nearer strip edge; right: the drift scan

cloud σ 100 µm

σ 150 µm

σ 200 µm

25

Details

A detector responds electron by electron, so a real pull moves each electron by where it lands (the "cloud-level" toy of the transfer slide does not; it is a shape check only). Per-electron pulls on σ 300–450 µm Gaussian clouds stay at a1 ≤ 0.04–0.07 with unchanged sharing (loop/toy_local.py).

Charged insulating gaps saturate at σ = ε₀E₀ ≈ 3.5 nC/cm² (39 kV/cm): then no field line ends on a gap and every gap electron lands on the nearer strip edge. With the quoted 540 µm strips that funnel gives a1 ≈ 0 (each gap feeds both edges). The sharing fixes only cloud width ⊗ induction: with a narrow electron cloud (σ 100–200 µm) and wide induction (350 µm; no-pull s1 0.59–0.67, the data’s range) the funnel onto narrow strips reaches a1 0.1–0.24 (loop/toy_funnel_regime.py).

A narrow cloud is plausible: a vertical track’s electrons are a depth mixture (30 mm gap), whose pitch-scale content is ~10× that of a Gaussian of the same rms, and attachment in the ~1 % H₂O gas at low drift field removes the deep electrons; the drift scan shows the Y share narrowing (0.98 → 0.56) as a1 rises.

Prediction tested: narrow strips (≲ 300 µm) with wide gaps on the June prints. The full sim says no. Paired arms vs the 550 µm control (36 angle/seed pairs each, 190 / 290 µm X kernels, matched funnel; paired_odd_narrow.json): odd amplitude ×0.21 (190 µm), ×0.59 (190 µm + funnel), ×0.52 (290 µm), ×0.92 (290 µm + funnel), against the ×2.5–5 needed; the funnel arms also narrow the sharing (Δs1 −0.05 … −0.10). In the full sim the asymmetry grows with strip width, opposite to the toy: the sim’s real depth-mixture clouds and resistive induction are not the toy’s narrow-cloud regime.

26

Details

Skewed X response: with uniform illumination, a1 ≠ 0 needs a response that is not mirror-symmetric about the pad. Registration gets there by attracting the charge (and pays with the even term). The other way is a weighting field that leans toward one neighbour, without moving the charge: the centroid shifts, the ±1 sum is unchanged at first order, and the pad type doesn’t matter. Offset strips acting as partly conducting electrodes in the induction are one way to get it, and a smooth two-signed lean would follow from the print registration. Only its static version was modelled (route 9, rejected on a class criterion now void, and because it grew with cloud size).

Surface charging: insulating surfaces (coverlay, gap kapton) on fresh June bulks charging up and adding a lateral field. It would naturally give time and field dependence, and an HV incident could reset it (6-19). It has no worked prediction for the map geometry or pad-pitch locking yet.

These are candidates to test, not results.

Update (FOLLOWUP §7): the skewed response is not untested after all. Every full-sim arm runs on W2 kernels whose X box is the 31.2 mm superperiod, so offset resistive strips at every δ are in them, and a 2-D floating-strip toy at the sim’s sharing gives the sim’s size (O ≈ 0.04). The one piece the sim lacked, avalanche ions returning along the funnel’s field lines, reduces the funnel’s asymmetry by 5–10 % (skew/ion_path_toy.py).

27

Details

The even-term score proposed earlier in this audit turned out not to discriminate (slide "Even term"): the sharing change of a pull runs both ways relative to an unpulled board, and bulk-local sharing structure is ±0.1. The shape of the transfer (±1 vs ±2) and the size are the scores that remain.

Step 6 is the most decisive physical measurement: registration predicts strip-centre offsets of opposite sign (±100–300 µm) in det2’s positive and negative bands, and a 780 µm pitch. A phone photo through a microscope eyepiece at a few points would do. Read strip width and gap too.

Analysis does not wait for the mechanism: wft.xasym (nTof_x17, commit 30198e4) corrects det2 and det3 June-15 positions with a measured map × per-run scale (K = −0.77 ± 0.13 vs M3). It removes a positional systematic of up to ±70 µm and leaves the resolution unchanged.

Where it stands

The effect is well measured and the analysis can be corrected. If the photographed film is the production print (761 µm), the resistive strips are ruled out as its cause

What is left

• A static (saturated) surface charge on fresh June bulks: gain-independent, unlike charging-up.

• Something in the pad / via layer of the June PCBs (pad-pitch locked by construction).

• The bulk process itself (mesh, pillars, lamination): Stephan says "nothing different".

• Something nobody has named yet: X-only, June only, set by the cloud width.

Open decisions

• Confirm the film is the production pattern at 1:1 (Dylan checking).

• Detector tests when access returns: collimated scan across a pad, HV ramps and dwell, dry gas.

• The sim’s strip imprint is ≥ 5–10× too strong: rework the strip response before trusting strip-based sim results?

• Adopt wft.xasym in production (needs a re-alignment and per-run scales)?

28
